title: Ephemeral GPU bleed: tombstone lockup + allocator coalescer runtime hotpatch
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + dedicated) reported sudden GPU OOM spikes during afternoon traffic windows over the last 2 weeks. Investigation shows concurrent tombstone compaction in the KV cache could leave dangling slab references under specific interleavings, preventing slab reuse and amplifying allocator fragmentation when long-sequence requests spike. The combined effect produces transient 'bleed' where total usable GPU memory drops and OOMs occur despite aggregate allocations being within quota. This ticket tracks a targeted runtime patch, rollout plan, and customer mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Can reproduce scenario with stress harness: interleaved tombstone compaction + tenant prefix churn + long-seq generation causing allocator fragmentation; 2) Patch prevents dangling references and coalesces freed blocks to avoid fragmentation on large tensor allocations; 3) Canary shows 90% reduction in OOM rate and no regression in latency P99; 4) Automated unit+stress tests added to CI; 5) Postmortem and customer communication completed.
root_cause_analysis:
- Race between kvcache tombstone sweeper and slab reuse allocator: tombstone sweep would mark entries but free paths did not synchronize with slab metadata updates, leaving internal slab pages marked in-use by stale handles.
- Allocator free path lacked coalescing for recently freed large contiguous tensor regions; repeated allocate/free of varying sizes produced fragmentation that prevented new ~2-4GB tensor reservations (common for long-context batches).
- Under tenant churn, these two issues amplified: leaked tombstone metadata reduced effective slab pool while fragmentation prevented compaction, causing rapid OOMs on peak requests.
proposed_fix:
1) Add explicit tombstone sweep fence: tombstone compaction now acquires light-weight per-arena epoch lock before removing index entries to eliminate handle races.
2) Implement deferred free list coalescer: freed regions are merged in background up to a configurable window to reduce immediate contention on hot allocation paths.
3) Add safety fallback: when contiguous large allocation fails, fallback path will attempt prefix-eviction heuristics before failing call.
4) Instrument additional metrics: slab_freeable_bytes, tombstone_pending_count, coalescer_backlog.
5) Ship as runtime-1.19.3 hotpatch with incremental canary rollout across hosted, then Dedicated pools, and lastly Private via customer-managed upgrade package.
mitigations_for_customers: Short-term mitigations customers can apply if experiencing OOMs: 1) Reduce max_batch_token and max_seq_length temporarily; 2) Set kvcache.eviction_threshold to 0.7 to force earlier evictions; 3) For Dedicated clusters, run ad-hoc tenant prefix sweep: curl -X POST /admin/evict-prefix; 4) Temporarily shift heavy long-context traffic to region fallback. Operational runbook attached in comments.
rollout_plan:
- Build and smoke test runtime-1.19.3 internally (QA + perf): 2025-11-18 to 2025-11-20
- Internal canary (10 nodes, low-traffic): 2025-11-21 to 2025-11-25
- Expanded canary (50 nodes, mixed traffic) monitor 7d: 2025-11-26 to 2025-12-02
- Hostedscale rollout with 5% increments if metrics stable: target complete 2025-12-09
- Dedicated customers: coordinate per-account; Private customers: provide package and notes.
Rollback: automated rollback flag + snapshot allocator indices before upgrade; if OOMs increase > baseline+10% or latency regress P99 > 15%, rollback immediate.
qa_and_tests:
- New stress harness reproducer added to runtime-infra-tests (run with --kv-churn --long-seq).
- Unit tests for tombstone fence semantics and allocator coalescer logic.
- Perf run to ensure coalescer background job CPU < 2% on default config.
- Integration test with Dedicated and Hosted multi-tenant config to validate live eviction heuristics.
postmortem_tasks: 1) Draft customer-facing incident report and notify impacted accounts; 2) Add continuous alert for tombstone_pending_count > 1000; 3) Review allocator design for next-phase rewrite (Q1 2026); 4) Close loop with SRE to add tenant-level circuit-breaker for allocation storms.
